title: Retire the web-URL audit skill and make bundle text name only live tools
summary: The bundled platform plugin still taught a retired capability. plugins/assayer/skills/assayer-audit described auditing a web URL through the browser runtime that this repository already removed, and its premise no longer has a provider: the only installed capability provider is assayer-document-navigation. The same file list also survived as a tracked duplicate under .agents/skills/assayer-audit. Two other user-facing files taught retired protocol names: plugins/assayer/skills/assayer-plugin told the Agent to drive start_plugin_run and advance_plugin_run, which scripts/check_architecture_boundaries.py classifies as removed plugin protocol fields, and assayer-plugin-lifecycle listed start_plugin_run and start_audit as current tools. plugins/assayer/.codex-plugin/plugin.json advertised an exact wheel, frontend issues, and the ass-spec plugin. The host CLI routed an http(s) target to the assayer-audit Skill and the raw transport module while routing every other target to the domain-plugin lifecycle server, so a web target took a second, now dead path. No gate looked at any of this text: check_architecture_boundaries.py scans only Python under src/ and packages/*/src, check_plugin_source_boundaries.py excluded plugins/assayer by design, and check_document_boundaries.py scans only docs/, so a retired tool name in a Skill was invisible while all gates stayed green. This change deletes the audit Skill and its duplicate, rewrites the plugin Skill to the compiled workflow (start_compiled_run through get_compiled_result, with the five-state verdict contract), repoints the lifecycle table and manifest prompts, makes the host CLI route every target through the same domain-plugin lifecycle server, and extends check_plugin_source_boundaries.py to police the platform bundle's authored text: a tool-shaped token must exist in the frozen live MCP tool set and retired protocol or decision vocabulary is rejected outright, with a test that keeps the frozen set equal to the transports' real surface. Verification evidence: the change landed in 73d046d, pushed on 2026-09-17 with 73d046d as the publish point, and CI run 35200240263 passed all seven jobs; locally the fast profile reported 439 tests OK and full reported 452 tests OK with the design confirmation, architecture, document, plugin-source, English text, and resilience gates returning 0; the expanded plugin-source gate rejects a planted start_plugin_run and a planted needs_review token and accepts live tool names such as list_plugins and plan_review_batches, and @assayer_rev independently re-ran the checks in a detached worktree, verified that the deleted Skill and its tracked duplicate are gone with no dangling reference, that the host CLI routes every target through one server configuration, and passed the semantic classification.

platform: Owns the host CLI target routing and the plugin-source boundary gate
plugin: Owns the bundled platform plugin manifest and Agent-facing Skills
provider: No provider change; the retired Skill is removed because no provider supplies its premise
agent: Agent guidance now teaches only the platform-owned compiled workflow

forbiddenResponsibilities: The Skills must not reintroduce a browser, web-URL, or frontend-specific premise
The Skills must not teach a tool name the compiled Host does not expose
The gate must not import the runtime to obtain the live tool set; it keeps a frozen set that a test reconciles with the transports
The gate must not scan generated runtime material or local build state as authored text
The batch must not touch the frozen v1 contracts, DECISION_STATES, schemas/common.schema.json, or historical records in docs/
acceptance: plugins/assayer/skills/assayer-audit and the tracked duplicate .agents/skills/assayer-audit no longer exist

every tool-shaped token in plugins/assayer authored text exists in the live MCP tool surface, and the compiled workflow steps in the plugin Skill match the transport: start_compiled_run, bind_provider, discover_sources, collect_evidence, plan_review_batches, submit_review_batch, finalize_compiled_run, get_compiled_result
scripts/check_plugin_source_boundaries.py returns 1 and names the offending token when a platform bundle Skill quotes a retired tool name such as start_plugin_run, and returns 0 on the current bundle
tests/test_plugin_source_boundaries.py proves the frozen live tool set still equals the union of the compiled and plugin-lifecycle transports' tools
the host CLI uses one server configuration for every target: an http(s) target and a markdown target produce the same command prefix and both prompt $assayer-plugin
no gate regresses: architecture, document, plugin-source, English text, design confirmation, and resilience all return 0, with the fast and full profiles passing

humanApproval.decision: Product-surface change carried out under the standing authorization of the refactor mandate in #assayer-group:4c84ee19 (approval time) and its delegation update: 于旸 stated that the agent and reviewer decide these changes themselves and that the workflow runs at most seven rounds, so no per-change sign-off is requested. The classification is semantic because the batch removes an Agent-facing Skill, repoints the manifest prompts, and changes how the host CLI routes a web target; @assayer_rev independently reviews the batch and proposed retiring the audit Skill instead of rewriting it, on the grounds that its web-URL premise is a removed capability, that assayer-document-navigation is the only provider, and that assayer-plugin already covers running any installed plugin.
